items.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He’s such a sweet piano player.

ctx.x: He’s such a sweet piano player.

His piano playing reflects him as a person, truly. But that’s so amazing. You talk about all these folks that we know as – they’re larger than life figures – and they’re all – they’re gentlemen. They have that humanity. There’s something there, either in the music or the musical culture, that seems to, if not nurture it, at least keep it alive. I think that that’s one of the things that attracted me to the music, and I think that it makes the music universally attractive to a lot of folks. Not everybody. Not…
Barron – are there any artists today that have caught your ear? I mean, there’s a plethora of musicians. Jason Moran has got a lot, and there’s . . .
